key_insight: An optimized gradient boosting decision tree predicted weld tensile strength with R² = 0.978 and identified process windows targeting at least 90% joint efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The approach provides a quantitative basis for selecting friction stir welding parameters for A7N01P-T4 aluminum alloy joints.
method: Predict ultimate tensile strength from rotational speed, welding speed, and shoulder plunge depth.
Compare baseline models, then tune gradient boosting with grid search.
Use SHAP to interpret parameter effects and map high-strength process windows.
evidence_signal: Using 27 experimental samples and leave-one-out cross-validation, reported R² improved from 0.905 for a decision tree to 0.966 for gradient boosting and 0.978 after tuning.
watch_item: The small dataset limits confidence in generalization; predicted process windows need independent experimental validation before production use.
paper_title: Interpretable ensemble learning for tensile strength prediction and welding process window optimization of friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum alloy
